channel.title: field/notes by Timothy Castillon
channel.description: A field record of the people and places carrying the weight of a changing world: labor, land, and the communities closest to both, documented up close and credited where I can.

item.title: Angkor: Stone, Water, and the Labor of Upkeep
item.description:
ANGKOR ARCHAEOLOGICAL PARK, SIEM REAP, KH, NOV 2026

I walked the rain slicked causeways at Angkor with a fun loving couple I had met, two people who share the same habit of staying out until the light fades. What stayed with me wasn't just the twelfth century stonework but the daily labor keeping it upright.

item.title: Zion: The Grandeur of Verticality
item.description:
ZION NATIONAL PARK, UT, SEP 2026

In Zion, the canyon walls pull your eyes straight up, though what stayed with me happened down along the trail. Walking beside my uncle, the sheer cliffs of Navajo sandstone felt untouchable until you notice the crowd lines and realize the quiet itself has to be rationed.

item.title: Valley of Fire: The Aesthetics of Aridity
item.description:
VALLEY OF FIRE, NV, APR 2026

I spent the afternoon out here with my uncle, and at one point he looked at the red Aztec sandstone and said it looked scorched, like the sun had been sitting on it too long. Watching visitors hurry back into air conditioned cars while park staff and road crews kept working in the glare, his remark stuck with me.

item.title: Atok: The Salad Bowl Above the Clouds
item.description:
ATOK, BENGUET, PH, JAN 2026

Driving up Halsema Highway before dawn past sheer rock overhangs, you watch steep mountain ridges give way to neat green rows of gulay that end up on Manila's tables the next morning. From Mount Olis, whole hillsides are terraced into cabbage, carrot, and potato plots, with tin roofed farmhouses tucked right beside the crops and trucks waiting along narrow cliffside turns.

item.title: Merkato: The Hide Trade of Addis Ababa
item.description:
ADDIS ABABA, ET, NOV 2025

At Merkato, the market runs on hands most of the city never stops to watch. Donkeys loaded with burlap sacks push through narrow alleys while hide sellers stretch raw qoda across wooden frames.

item.title: Crete: Stone, Salt, and Summer Light
item.description:
CHANIA, GEORGIOUPOLI, LAKE KOURNAS & TRIOPETRA, CRETE, GR, JUL 2025

In Crete, everything sits where dry rock meets open water. I came in summer with friends, and it was hot.

item.title: Islas Ballestas: The Poor Man's Galápagos
item.description:
ISLAS BALLESTAS, PE, JUN 2025

Islas Ballestas is built on what nests there: sea lions crowding the harbor buoys, Humboldt penguins, and dense colonies of seabirds whose droppings once drove Peru's nineteenth century guano boom before the islands became a marine reserve. Now the boats run on day trippers instead, steered by local captains whose income rises and falls with an ocean they cannot control.

item.title: Vinicunca: Life on the Rainbow Mountain
item.description:
VINICUNCA, PE, MAR 2025

Everyone climbs Vinicunca for the striped ridge, while the local families working the trail carry the real weight of keeping the mountain running. One of the kids offered me a ride up on his horse.

item.title: Cabrillo: Cliffs at the Edge of the Harbor
item.description:
POINT LOMA, SAN DIEGO, CA, US, OCT 2024

On the tip of Point Loma, two coastlines sit back to back. Look east from the ridge and San Diego Bay is packed with naval ships, runways, and concrete piers.

item.title: New York City: Concrete, Harbor, and Unpredictable Skies
item.description:
NEW YORK CITY, NY, US, APR 2024

Tourism in New York doesn't stop for the weather, even when the sky turns sideways. In April 2024, one day opened clear over Times Square and the stone facade of the Met, and the next dropped cold rain and sleet across the East River.

item.title: Grindelwald: The Architecture of Instability
item.description:
GRINDELWALD, CH, MAR 2024

From the valley floor in Grindelwald, the north face of the Eiger looks permanent, carved out of solid rock and ice. Up on the lifts, the mountain feels much less settled.

item.title: Lavaux: The Mirror of Lake Geneva
item.description:
SAINT-SAPHORIN & CHEXBRES, CH, MAY 2023

In Lavaux, the vineyards sit on steep stone terraces stacked by hand over centuries above Lake Geneva. I walked up from Saint-Saphorin toward Chexbres with coworkers for Caves Ouvertes, the spring cellar festival, stopping at small stone doorways along the slope.

item.title: Bethlehem & the Judean Hills: Stone, Faith, and Quiet
item.description:
BETHLEHEM & JERUSALEM, WEST BANK, JAN 2023

Looking up inside the dome at the Chapel of the Shepherds' Field in Beit Sahour, with light filtering through the ceiling above the nativity frescoes, there is a stillness that stays with you long after you step back out into the bright limestone streets. Outside, the city spreads across pale terraced hillsides before dropping abruptly into the dry, bare folds of the Judean Desert, where flags snap against utility poles in the wind.

item.title: Nice: Coastline at Low Tide
item.description:
NICE, FR, OCT 2022

Pastel shutters and iron balconies share a block with the coastal road without much friction, though most of my time here went to the shore. We woke up a bit late at the hotel and rushed down to the water for a quick, slow dip, sharing the shoreline with a few locals already in the sea.

item.title: Berat: Stone Walls and Sidewalk Looms
item.description:
BERAT, AL, AUG 2022

In Berat, daily trade happens right on the walls of the old town. Walking the steep cobblestone lanes toward the citadel, you pass hand knitted wool socks and vests hung on arched doorways, embroidered dresses clipped to wire lines, and woven kilim rugs draped over limestone masonry.

item.title: Mombasa: Tides, Reefs, and the Beach Economy
item.description:
BAMBURI, NYALI & MOMBASA, KE, APR 2022

Along the coast in Mombasa, the beach is both a resort backdrop and a crowded workplace. Walk down to the bahari at low tide and the whole informal economy is laid out on the sand: handlers leading camels for tourist photos, boat crews waiting beside glass bottom reef cruisers, fishermen hauling wooden ngalawa canoes through the shallows by hand.
